title: Utilities for ggplot2
text: Small, reusable utilities ggplot2. ggutils adds helpers plug usual grammar – new geometry, special data format – plot keeps plot. one solves concrete problem documented runnable examples. inside: guide_axis_smart() – readable labels crowded axes: pick labels (, n), spread several rows / columns without overlap, tie every label back tick leader line. guide_axis_cluster() / scale_x_cluster() / scale_y_cluster() – hierarchical clustering axes: axis ordered dendrogram tree drawn next , one tree per panel free facets. coord_radial() plot theta tree becomes ring dendrogram (inside hole outside circle) partial arc gets arc-shaped r-axis tree. facet_gridn() – facet_grid() scales free per panel instead per row / column. coord_spiral() – Archimedean spiral coordinate matching angle radial axes, long sequences otherwise need many rows. Data layout helpers – bundled airway_heatmap, pbmc3k_markers pbmc3k_dotplot data, plus exported layout algorithms smart_align(), box_arrange() smart_stack().

title: Processed RNA-seq expression matrix (GEO GSE52778) — airway_heatmap

title: Spiral coordinates for ggplot2 — coord_spiral
text: coord_spiral() bends normal Cartesian ggplot Archimedean spiral, following geometry used spiralize package: base spiral r = b * theta b chosen one turn one radius unit.  x aesthetic runs along spiral (angle) y aesthetic runs across track (radius).  Points, lines, bars areas supported, facets get one spiral per panel.

title: Spiral coordinates for ggplot2 — coord_spiral
text: start, end Angular range spiral, degrees (spiralize::spiral_initialize()). 360 * n + convenient way ask n turns ending angle . turns Number turns, shortcut end = start + 360 * turns. supplied wins end, coord_spiral(turns = 5) always draws five turns whatever default end . period Number x units per turn. supplied, end recalculated x range period. clockwise Draw spiral clockwise? FALSE (default) draws counter-clockwise, like spiralize(). inner, outer Inner outer radius whole spiral, panel npc units (0.5 panel edge). Together set much panel spiral covers; distance two turns follows number turns. height Thickness data track, fraction distance two neighbouring turns (0 1): 0.7 leaves 30% white gap. gap knob way round, pick whichever reads better; gap wins given. gap White gap two neighbouring turns, fraction distance (0 1). gap = 0.3 height = 0.7. scale_by "angle" maps equal differences x equal differences angle; "curve" maps equal distances along spiral curve. reverse Reverse y direction inside track? flip One "none", "horizontal", "vertical", ""; mirrors whole spiral. labels Draw x (angle) y (radial) axis labels along spiral? y_axis Draw radial (y) axis ruler well angle axis? y_axis_theta Angle degrees radial ruler placed; NULL follows side scale_y_spiral_axis() (end spiral default).  Ignored scale sets axis_at. y_axis_n Number ticks radial ruler y scale breaks . clip Clipping panel, passed ggplot2. xlim, ylim Limits passed coord (usually set scales).

title: Spiral coordinates for ggplot2 — coord_spiral
text: coordinate draws axes .  ticks kept short enough sit inside white gap two neighbouring turns, labels stay just outside ticks, number radial labels follows thickness track, thin track gets fewer instead pile overlapping text. Every position aesthetic warped, x y: xend / yend, xmin / xmax ymin / ymax mapped formula.  geom_segment() (arrows included), geom_rect(), geom_ribbon() geom_boxplot() land track, although edge two warped points still straight line.  Layers without end points (geom_hline(), geom_vline(), geom_abline()) supported. Use scale_x_spiral_axis() scale_y_spiral_axis() change axes sit, long ticks labels turned; otherwise behave like ordinary continuous scales.

"bottom" / "top" (x axis): labels.  facets tree moved strip band, .e. directly strip panel, strip, tree, labels panel never overlap.  Use strip_side = "" draw outside strip instead; either way small gap (options(ggutils.tree_gap = 0.14), centimetres) keeps branches touching strip. "left" / "right" (y axis): left labels, far end panel row.  facets, "left" draws one tree per visible y axis; "right" draws one end every panel row. tree sit away labels travel axis guide (discrete secondary axis carry free panel's categories), drawn straight finished gtable, panel geometry known.  also makes facet_grid() work: row facet owns y axis column facet owns x axis, tree attached strip cell.

title: Cluster axis guide for ggplot2 — guide_axis_cluster
text: scales argument facet_wrap() / facet_grid() read automatically, free never written hand: "fixed": one shared tree every panel. "free_x": panel column gets x tree. "free_y": y trees recomputed per panel row. "free": axes recomputed panel panel. facet_wrap() draws one x tree per panel row (strip) one y tree per visible y axis; facet_grid() draws one x tree per panel one y tree per row.  Writing free = FALSE forces single shared tree, free = TRUE forces per-panel trees regardless scales.

Leave plot.margin / device room tree. r axis (y) – partial arcs .  full circle r axis plain column, scale_y_cluster() draws tree .  partial arc (start/end) ggplot2 puts r labels radial ray tree becomes arc-shaped wedge dendrogram end arc, side without labels: leaf position becomes radius merge height angle, every straight branch becomes concentric arc tree hugs heat map.  height sets angular width (min(pi/3, 0.30 * height) radians). code: # per-sample z-scores: standardise every sample across the genes once z <- local({   m <- tapply(airway_heatmap$df$z,               list(airway_heatmap$df$gene, airway_heatmap$df$sample), mean)   m <- scale(m)                                # column-wise = per sample   out <- as.data.frame(as.table(m))   names(out) <- c("gene", "sample", "z_sample")   merge(out, airway_heatmap$genes[c("gene", "gene_set")], by = "gene") }) d <- droplevels(z[z$gene %in% unique(z$gene)[1:16], ]) fill_scale <- scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166ac", mid = "white",                                    high = "#b2182b", midpoint = 0,                                    name = "z (sample)")  # (1) x tree inside the hole: bottom + inner.radius ggplot(d, aes(gene, sample, fill = z_sample)) + geom_tile() +   coord_radial(theta = "x", inner.radius = 0.55) +   scale_x_cluster(method = "ward.D2", height = 1.2) +   fill_scale  # (2) x tree outside the circle: position = "top" ggplot(d, aes(gene, sample, fill = z_sample)) + geom_tile() +   coord_radial(theta = "x") +   scale_x_cluster(method = "ward.D2", height = 1, position = "top") +   fill_scale  # (3) partial arc + r-axis tree at the label-free end of the arc ggplot(d, aes(gene, sample, fill = z_sample)) + geom_tile() +   coord_radial(theta = "x", start = -0.5 * pi, end = 0.5 * pi,                inner.radius = 0.55) +   scale_y_cluster(method = "ward.D2", height = 1.6) +   fill_scale  # (4) facetted: one tree per panel, clustered per panel ggplot(d, aes(gene, sample, fill = z_sample)) + geom_tile() +   facet_wrap(~ gene_set, scales = "free_x") +   coord_radial(theta = "x", inner.radius = 0.45) +   scale_x_cluster(method = "ward.D2", height = 0.8) +   fill_scale +   theme_grey(base_size = 7)

code: library(ggplot2)  d <- data.frame(   sample = factor(paste0("S", 1:40)),   value  = rnorm(40) )  # 40 categories: labels are spread over several rows and connected to # their ticks with leader lines ggplot(d, aes(sample, value)) +   geom_point() +   scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis_smart())   # only a hand-picked subset of labels is displayed ggplot(d, aes(sample, value)) +   geom_point() +   scale_x_discrete(     guide = guide_axis_smart(which = c("S1", "S10", "S20", "S30", "S40"))   )   # on a vertical axis the labels are stacked in columns ggplot(d, aes(value, sample)) +   geom_point() +   scale_y_discrete(guide = guide_axis_smart(which = c("S1", "S20", "S40")))   # `coord_radial()` (ggplot2 >= 3.5) names the position scales `theta` and `r`; # attach the guide with `guides(theta = ...)` and it draws the selected labels # along the ring, like `guide_axis_theta()` ggplot(d, aes(sample, value)) +   geom_col() +   coord_radial(theta = "x") +   guides(theta = guide_axis_smart(which = seq(1, 40, by = 4)))   # the categories can also be the `theta` scale when they are mapped to y ggplot(d, aes(value, sample)) +   geom_col() +   coord_radial(theta = "y") +   guides(theta = guide_axis_smart(n = 10))   # a crowded run of labels is spread along the arc and connected to its ticks # with the three-segment leader lines ggplot(d, aes(sample, value)) +   geom_col() +   coord_radial(theta = "x") +   guides(theta = guide_axis_smart(which = 9:20))   # only part of the circle (a half circle) works the same ggplot(d, aes(sample, value)) +   geom_col() +   coord_radial(theta = "x", start = -0.5 * pi, end = 0.5 * pi) +   guides(theta = guide_axis_smart(which = 9:20))   # heat maps below use per-sample z-scores: each sample standardised across # the 300 genes of the bundled matrix z_sample <- as.data.frame(as.table(scale(   tapply(airway_heatmap$df$z,          list(airway_heatmap$df$gene, airway_heatmap$df$sample), mean) ))) names(z_sample) <- c("gene", "sample", "z_sample") z_sample <- merge(z_sample, airway_heatmap$genes[c("gene", "gene_set")],                   by = "gene")  # a circular heatmap from the bundled RNA-seq data (300 genes x 8 samples): # the genes run around the circle, labels outside data(airway_heatmap) ggplot(z_sample, aes(gene, sample, fill = z_sample)) +   geom_tile() +   coord_radial(theta = "x", inner.radius = 0.2) +   guides(theta = guide_axis_smart(which = airway_heatmap$mark)) +   scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166ac", mid = "white", high = "#b2182b",                        midpoint = 0, name = "z-score (sample)")   # the same heatmap with the labels attached to the inner radius (inside the # hole); a large inner radius leaves room for them ggplot(z_sample, aes(gene, sample, fill = z_sample)) +   geom_tile() +   coord_radial(theta = "x", inner.radius = 0.62) +   guides(theta = guide_axis_smart(     which = airway_heatmap$mark, theta_side = "inside"   )) +   scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166ac", mid = "white", high = "#b2182b",                        midpoint = 0, name = "z-score (sample)")   # with facets every panel is a circle of its own d_facet <- data.frame(   panel = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 20),   cat   = factor(rep(paste0("g", 1:20), 2), levels = paste0("g", 1:20)),   value = rnorm(40) ) ggplot(d_facet, aes(cat, value)) +   geom_col(fill = "#3b82f6") +   coord_radial(theta = "x") +   guides(theta = guide_axis_smart(which = seq(1, 20, by = 2))) +   facet_wrap(~panel)   # a faceted circular heatmap needs scales = "free_x": each panel then has its # own gene scale, so the ring is complete and only that panel's genes are # labelled ggplot(z_sample, aes(gene, sample, fill = z_sample)) +   geom_tile() +   coord_radial(theta = "x", inner.radius = 0.3) +   guides(theta = guide_axis_smart(which = unlist(airway_heatmap$mark_by_set))) +   facet_wrap(~gene_set, ncol = 2, scales = "free_x") +   scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166ac", mid = "white", high = "#b2182b",                        midpoint = 0, name = "z-score (sample)")
